Overview: Dengue is endemic in more than 100 countries around the world, with nearly half the world's population at risk of infected dengue.
Symptoms: Dengue fever typically presents with a wide spectrum of symptoms, ranging from asymptomatic infection to severe disease. Severe dengue fever is characterized by specific warning signs that indicate a higher risk of adverse outcomes. Severe dengue is characterized by hemorrhagic and inflammatory complications.
Causes: Dengue is caused by infection with one of the four serotypes of the dengue virus (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, and DENV-4) primarily through the bite of infected *Aedes aegypti* mosquitoes . Dengue is transmitted primarily through the bite of infected female *Aedes albopictus* mosquitoes . After an extrinsic incubation period within the mosquito, the virus can then be transmitted to other humans through the bite of infected *Aedes aegypti* mosquitoes .
Treatment: Dengue is a viral ailment characterized primarily by fever, dehydration, and dehydration. Treatment is supportive, focusing on symptom alleviation and careful monitoring to prevent progression to severe disease. Patients at higher risk include pregnant individuals, elderly, and those with chronic conditions.
When to See a Doctor: Prompt medical attention is critical for effective dengue management, as early diagnosis and timely intervention can significantly reduce mortality rates in well-managed settings
